topic_title: Future Tense Mastery + SBI PO Level Error Detection

intro_payload.title: Future Tense — Zero to Officer Level
intro_payload.subtitle: SBI PO / BPSC / SSC / Railway Error Detection Special
learning_outcomes: Simple Future, Future Continuous, Future Perfect, Future Perfect Continuous — full mastery
Shall vs Will — the traditional rule and modern exam usage
Going to vs Will — planned intention vs spontaneous decision vs evidence-based prediction
Present Continuous & Simple Present used for future (schedules & plans)
Time/Conditional Clauses — the 'No Future Tense' trap (if/when/before/after/until)
Future in the Past (would, was/were going to) & Reported Speech backshift
SBI PO / BPSC style sentence error-detection practice with real traps

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Sir, kal main apne cousin ke ghar JAAUNGA, wahan sabse milunga.

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Achha bataya Raju! Notice karo — 'jaaunga', 'milunga' — dono words batate hain ki kaam abhi tak hua nahi hai, aage hoga.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Haan sir, kal ki baat hai, abhi to main yahin hoon.

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Bilkul sahi! Jab bhi hum kisi kaam ke baare mein baat karte hain jo ABHI NAHI hua, aage hoga, uske liye English mein ek special tense hota hai. Chalo dekhte hain.

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Raju, Hindi grammar mein tumne 'Bhavishya Kaal' padha hoga — jo aane wale samay mein hoga, uske liye.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Haan sir! 'Main kal school jaunga' ya 'Kal baarish hogi' jaisa?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Ekdum sahi examples! English mein isko 'Future Tense' kehte hain. Jab bhi verb ke saath 'unga, egi, enge' jaisa Hindi word ho, samjho Future Tense hai.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Achhaaaa! Toh 'main aaunga' bhi future hi hoga?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Bilkul Raju! Future Tense ke bhi 4 types hote hain — Simple Future, Future Continuous, Future Perfect, aur Future Perfect Continuous. Bilkul waise hi jaise Past aur Present Tense ke 4-4 types the.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Hain?? Isme bhi char types? Sir ye to exam me pakka confuse karega, itna kuch yaad rakhna padega!

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Tension mat lo, aur ek acchi baat — Future Tense mein 'will/shall' word hamesha common rehta hai, bas uske baad ki verb ka form badalta hai. Pattern samajh gaye to easy ho jaayega.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Chaliye sir, sabse pehla wala shuru karte hain!

guess_payload.question: Raju, guess karo — inme se kaunsa sentence FUTURE TENSE dikhata hai?
guess_payload.explanation: Sahi jawab C hai! 'Will' ek helping verb hai jo future action dikhati hai, aur 'tomorrow' ek future time marker hai — dono milkar confirm karte hain ki ye Future Tense hai.

quiz_payload.question: Future Tense ke kitne main types hote hain?
quiz_payload.explanation: Chaar types: Simple Future, Future Continuous, Future Perfect, Future Perfect Continuous — Past aur Present Tense jaisa hi structure hai.

quiz_payload.question: 'Bhavishya Kaal' English grammar ke kis concept se match karta hai?
quiz_payload.explanation: 'Bhavishya Kaal' ka English mein equivalent 'Future Tense' hai — jo aane wale samay mein hoga, uske liye use hota hai.

quiz_payload.question: Future Tense mein sabse common helping verb kaunsa hota hai?
quiz_payload.explanation: 'Will/Shall' Future Tense ka core helping verb hai, jo sabhi 4 types mein alag-alag combinations mein use hota hai — will+V1, will be+V-ing, will have+V3, will have been+V-ing.

milestone_payload.title: MODULE COMPLETED!
milestone_payload.motivational_quote: Foundation strong hai! Ab Simple Future ki deep dive karte hain — shall vs will ka bada trap wahin hai.

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Simple Future Tense use hota hai jab koi kaam future mein hoga, bina koi duration ya completion detail ke. Structure: Subject + will/shall + V1 (base form).

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Matlab jaise 'I will play cricket tomorrow' — bas 'will' laga do?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Bilkul sahi Raju! Aur dhyan rakhna, 'will/shall' ke baad hamesha V1 (base form) aati hai, kabhi V2 ya V3 nahi.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Toh 'I will played' bolna galat hoga?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: ⭐ Bilkul galat hoga, sirf V1 aayega. Ab suno traditional grammar rule jo BPSC bahut poochta hai — Shall FIRST PERSON (I, We) ke saath aata hai, Will baaki sab (You, He, She, It, They) ke saath.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Hain?? Toh 'He shall go' galat hoga aur 'I will go' bhi galat?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Traditional British grammar mein haan — 'I/We shall go', 'He/She/They will go' sahi maana jaata hai. Lekin modern usage mein 'will' sabke saath chal jaata hai, ye zyada common hai.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Toh exam mein konsa follow karun sir, confusion ho raha hai!

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: ⭐ BPSC ka favourite trap suno — 'Shall' ke 2 SPECIAL uses hain jo hamesha sahi maane jaate hain, in dono mein 'will' galat hoga: 1) Formal offers/suggestions with I/We — 'Shall we begin the meeting?', 'Shall I help you?'

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Aur dusra use, sir?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: 2) STRONG DETERMINATION, PROMISE, ya COMMAND jab subject SECOND/THIRD person ho — 'You shall not pass!' (strict order), 'He shall complete this task' (strong promise/threat). Yahan 'shall' obligation/command dikhata hai.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Achhaaaa! Toh offers mein 'shall I/we', aur strong warning/promise mein 'shall you/he/they' — ye dono exceptions hain!

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Ab contractions aur negative form dekho: 'Will not' = 'Won't', 'Shall not' = 'Shan't'. 'I won't go there' sahi hai.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Sir 'willn't' jaisa kuch bhi hota hai kya?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Nahi Raju, 'willn't' ek non-existent word hai — exam mein ye ek common wrong option ke roop mein daala jaata hai. Sirf 'won't' hi sahi contraction hai.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Note kar liya — will not = won't (spelling bhi alag hai 'wo' se shuru), shall not = shan't!

quiz_payload.question: Kaunsa sentence sahi hai? (Formal offer context)

options.text: Will I open the window for you?
Shall I open the window for you?
Do I open the window for you?
Am I open the window for you?

quiz_payload.explanation: Formal offers/suggestions ke liye 'Shall I/we' use hota hai, ye ek special exception hai jahan 'will' use nahi hota.

quiz_payload.question: 'Will not' ka sahi contraction kya hai?
quiz_payload.explanation: 'Will not' ka sahi contraction 'Won't' hai. 'Willn't' English mein exist hi nahi karta — ye common spelling trap hai.

quiz_payload.question: Error Detection: 'The workers (A)/ will worked overtime (B)/ to finish the project (C)/ No error (D)'
quiz_payload.explanation: 'Will' ke baad hamesha V1 (base form) aati hai, V2 nahi. Sahi: 'will work overtime', 'will worked' galat hai.

milestone_payload.title: MODULE COMPLETED!
milestone_payload.motivational_quote: Shall vs Will ka trap crack kar diya! Ab dekhte hain 'Going to' aur 'Will' mein kya farak hai.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Sir, maine kal hi decide kiya tha ki weekend pe movie dekhne jaunga. Isko kaise likhenge?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Badhiya sawal Raju! Jab koi plan PEHLE SE DECIDE ho chuka ho (kal decide kiya, aaj bata rahe ho), tab 'be going to + V1' use hota hai — 'I am going to watch a movie this weekend.'

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Matlab 'will' use nahi karenge isme?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Bilkul sahi! Ye pehla bada difference hai — 'Going to' = PEHLE SE PLAN kiya hua kaam. 'Will' = ABHI, ISI WAQT liya gaya decision.

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Socho Raju — tumhara phone baj raha hai aur tum bolte ho 'Ruko, main uthata hoon' — ye decision tumne USI PAL liya, koi pehle se plan nahi tha.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Haan sir, ye toh turant ka decision hai!

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Yahi hai 'Will' ka main use — SPONTANEOUS/instant decisions, promises, aur offers. 'I will answer the phone.' Isme koi planning nahi hai, bas turant faisla liya.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Achhaaaa! Toh 'will' = turant ka faisla, 'going to' = pehle se socha hua plan — clear ho gaya!

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: ⭐ Ab sabse bada exam trap suno — PREDICTIONS ke liye bhi dono use hote hain, par farak hai EVIDENCE ka. Agar prediction sirf OPINION/belief pe based ho — 'will' use hota hai: 'I think it will rain tomorrow.'

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Aur agar EVIDENCE dikh raha ho, jaise kaale baadal?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: ⭐ BILKUL SAHI! Jab PRESENT EVIDENCE dekh ke prediction karte hain — 'going to' use hota hai: 'Look at those dark clouds, it is going to rain!' Yahan clouds ek visible proof hai.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Toh 'will' = bina proof ka guess, 'going to' = saamne dikh raha proof — ye toh SBI PO ka top favourite trap lagta hai!

guess_payload.question: Raju, guess karo — kaunsa sentence sahi context mein hai? 'Dekho, wo car full speed mein deewar ki taraf ja rahi hai!'

options.text: The car will hit the wall!
The car is going to hit the wall!
The car shall hit the wall!

guess_payload.explanation: Yahan present evidence (car deewar ki taraf ja rahi hai) saamne dikh raha hai, isliye 'going to' use hoga, 'will' nahi. Evidence-based prediction ka ye classic example hai.

quiz_payload.question: 'I ___ visit my grandmother next month, I decided this last week.' Sahi form chuno:
quiz_payload.explanation: 'Last week decide kiya' — ye ek pehle se socha hua plan hai, isliye 'am going to' aayega, spontaneous 'will' nahi.

quiz_payload.question: Error Detection: 'The doorbell is ringing (A)/ wait, I am going to (B)/ open the door (C)/ No error (D)'
quiz_payload.explanation: Doorbell abhi bajी, isliye ye ek SPONTANEOUS decision hai (koi pehle se plan nahi tha). Sahi: 'I will open the door', 'am going to' galat context hai.

quiz_payload.question: Evidence-based prediction ke liye kaunsi structure sahi hai?
quiz_payload.explanation: Jab present mein visible proof/evidence ke basis pe prediction ki jaaye (jaise kaale baadal dekh ke), 'going to' use hota hai, 'will' nahi.

milestone_payload.title: MODULE COMPLETED!
milestone_payload.motivational_quote: Evidence trap crack kar diya! Ab dekhte hain Present Tense se bhi Future kaise bataya jaata hai.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Sir, mera dost bolta hai 'I am meeting him tomorrow' — but isme 'am' hai, 'will' nahi hai! Ye galat nahi hai kya?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Nahi Raju, bilkul sahi hai! Ye ek special use hai — FIXED PERSONAL ARRANGEMENTS/plans ke liye Present Continuous (is/am/are+V-ing) future ke liye bhi use hota hai.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Matlab 'am meeting' aur 'am going to meet' dono same meaning denge?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Bahut close hain, dono mein plan/arrangement dikhta hai. Farak itna hai ki Present Continuous mein usually koi specific time/place bhi FIXED hota hai — jaise appointment, ticket booked, confirmed meeting.

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Ab teesra tarika dekho — jab kaam FIXED TIMETABLE/schedule ke hisaab se ho (train, flight, school), tab Simple Present use hota hai — 'The train leaves at 6 PM tomorrow.'

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Hain?? Ye toh Present Tense wale chapter mein bhi padha tha maine!

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Bilkul sahi yaad hai! Ye rule dono chapters mein common hai kyunki ye Present Tense ka hi ek special FUTURE MEANING wala use hai. Official/fixed schedule = Simple Present.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Achha! Toh personal plan = Present Continuous, official timetable = Simple Present — dono future ke liye but alag context!

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: ⭐ Ab poora future-expression ka chart yaad karo: 1) Will = spontaneous decision/opinion-prediction. 2) Going to = pre-decided plan/evidence-based prediction. 3) Present Continuous = fixed personal arrangement. 4) Simple Present = official timetable.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Sir ye chaaron itne close hain, exam mein mix ho jaayenge!

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Isiliye hamesha CONTEXT dekho — kaam kab decide hua, proof hai ya nahi, personal hai ya official schedule. Context hi tumhe sahi form batayega.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Theek hai sir, main context pe focus karunga, sirf word pe nahi!

quiz_payload.question: 'The Rajdhani Express ___ Patna at 5 AM sharp.' Sahi form chuno (fixed railway schedule):
quiz_payload.explanation: Fixed official timetable (railway schedule) ke liye Simple Present use hota hai — 'The Rajdhani Express leaves Patna at 5 AM sharp'.

quiz_payload.question: Error Detection: 'I (A)/ am meet the Principal (B)/ at 10 AM tomorrow regarding admission (C)/ No error (D)'
quiz_payload.explanation: Present Continuous ka structure 'am/is/are + V-ing' hai. Sahi: 'I am meeting the Principal', 'am meet' galat structure hai.

quiz_payload.question: Fixed personal arrangement (already booked/confirmed plan) ke liye kaunsa tense use hota hai?
quiz_payload.explanation: Fixed personal arrangements (jaise ticket booked ho, appointment fix ho) ke liye Present Continuous use hota hai — 'I am flying to Delhi next week.'

milestone_payload.title: MODULE COMPLETED!
milestone_payload.motivational_quote: 4-way future chart yaad ho gaya! Ab Future Continuous ki taraf chalte hain.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Sir, agar main kal 5 baje SO RAHA HOUNGA jab aap ghar aayenge, isko kya bolenge?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Bahut badhiya example Raju! 'So raha hounga' — matlab kaam FUTURE ke ek PARTICULAR TIME pe CHAL RAHA hoga, khatam nahi hoga. Isko Future Continuous Tense kehte hain.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Toh ye bilkul Past Continuous jaisa hi hai bas future mein?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Bilkul sahi comparison! Jaise Past Continuous mein 'was/were+V-ing' tha, waise hi yahan 'will be+V-ing' hoga.

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Structure: Subject + will be + V-ing. 'I will be sleeping at 5 PM tomorrow when you arrive.' Sabhi subjects ke saath 'will be' same rehta hai.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Toh 'is/am/are' ki tension nahi hai isme, sirf 'will be' fix hai?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Bilkul sahi! 'Will be' sabhi subjects (I/You/He/They) ke saath same rehta hai, bas verb 'ing' form mein aati hai.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Achha! Toh 'He will be sleeping' aur 'They will be sleeping' — dono mein 'will be' hi rahega!

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Future Continuous ke 2 main uses yaad rakho: 1) Action jo ek PARTICULAR future moment pe chal rahi hogi — 'At 8 PM, I will be watching TV.'

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Aur dusra use, sir?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: 2) POLITE QUESTIONS ya casual inquiries about someone's plans — 'Will you be joining us for dinner?' Ye 'Will you join' se zyada polite/soft sunai deta hai.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Achhaaaa! Toh polite tareeke se poochne ke liye bhi ye use hota hai — interesting hai ye!

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: ⭐ Ek important trap suno — Future Continuous mein stative verbs (know, love, want, believe) bhi use nahi hoti, kyunki wo hamesha continuous form avoid karti hain, chahe koi bhi tense ho.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Toh 'I will be knowing the result tomorrow' galat hoga?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: ⭐ Bilkul sahi pakda! Ye exam ka common trap hai. Sahi hoga: 'I will know the result tomorrow' — Simple Future, 'will be knowing' galat hai kyunki 'know' stative verb hai.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Ohh! Toh stative verb ka rule sabhi continuous tenses mein same rehta hai — Present, Past, aur Future teeno mein!

quiz_payload.question: Sahi sentence chuno:

options.text: This time tomorrow, I will fly to Mumbai.
This time tomorrow, I will be flying to Mumbai.
This time tomorrow, I am flying to Mumbai always.
This time tomorrow, I will been flying to Mumbai.

quiz_payload.explanation: 'This time tomorrow' ek particular future moment dikhata hai jab action in-progress hogi — Future Continuous 'will be flying' sahi structure hai.

quiz_payload.question: Error Detection: 'I (A)/ will be believing you (B)/ once you show proof (C)/ No error (D)'
quiz_payload.explanation: 'Believe' ek stative verb hai, isliye continuous form nahi lagti. Sahi: 'I will believe you'.

quiz_payload.question: 'Will you be attending the wedding next week?' — ye sentence kis purpose ke liye use ho raha hai?
quiz_payload.explanation: Future Continuous ka ek use POLITE questions/inquiries poochne ke liye hota hai jo 'Will you attend' se zyada soft sunai deta hai.

milestone_payload.title: MODULE COMPLETED!
milestone_payload.motivational_quote: Bahut badhiya Raju! Ab dekhte hain future mein 'khatam ho chuka' kaam kaise likhte hain — Future Perfect!

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Sir, 'Jab tak aap aayenge, main apna homework KAR CHUKA HOUNGA' — ye kaunsa tense hoga?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Bahut sundar example Raju! 'Kar chuka hounga' — matlab ek future point tak ye kaam COMPLETE ho chuka hoga. Isko Future Perfect Tense kehte hain.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Matlab ye bataata hai ki future ke ek time se PEHLE kaam khatam ho jaayega?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Bilkul sahi! Future Perfect ek future action ko dikhata hai jo ek DUSRE future event/time se PEHLE COMPLETE ho jaayega.

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Structure: Subject + will have + V3 (past participle). 'I will have finished my homework by the time you arrive.'

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Toh 'V3' wahi hai jo Past Perfect aur Present Perfect mein bhi use hoti thi?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Bilkul sahi yaad rakha! V3 same rehti hai, bas helping verb badalta hai — had+V3 (Past Perfect), have/has+V3 (Present Perfect), will have+V3 (Future Perfect).

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Achha! Toh 'go' ka V3 'gone' hoga — 'She will have gone' sahi, 'She will have went' galat!

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: ⭐ Ek zaroori trigger word yaad rakho — 'By' ya 'By the time' + future point. 'By 2030, scientists will have found a cure.' 'By the time we reach, the show will have started.'

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Sir 'by the time' toh Past Perfect wale chapter mein bhi tha, wahan Simple Past aata tha na?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: ⭐ Bahut acha observation! Ye BPSC ka bada trap hai — agar dono events FUTURE mein hain, to 'by the time' clause mein SIMPLE PRESENT aayega (future meaning ke liye), aur main clause mein Future Perfect. 'By the time he arrives, we will have left.'

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: ⭐ Ohh! Toh 'by the time' ke saath future context mein 'arrives' (Simple Present) hi aayega, 'will arrive' nahi — same jaisa time-clause rule!

quiz_payload.question: Sahi sentence chuno:

options.text: By the time you will reach the station, the train will have left.
By the time you reach the station, the train will have left.
By the time you reach the station, the train had left.
By the time you reached the station, the train will have left.

quiz_payload.explanation: 'By the time' clause mein future meaning ke liye Simple Present aata hai ('reach'), aur main clause mein Future Perfect ('will have left') aata hai.

quiz_payload.question: Error Detection: 'By next year (A)/ she will have complete (B)/ her graduation (C)/ No error (D)'
quiz_payload.explanation: 'Will have' ke baad V3 (past participle) aata hai, 'complete' ka V3 'completed' hai. Sahi: 'will have completed'.

quiz_payload.question: Future Perfect Tense kab use hota hai?

options.text: Jab kaam abhi ho raha ho
Jab kaam future ke ek point tak complete ho jaayega
Jab kaam past mein complete ho chuka ho

quiz_payload.explanation: Future Perfect ek future action ko dikhata hai jo ek dusre future time/event se PEHLE complete ho jaayega — 'will have + V3'.

milestone_payload.title: MODULE COMPLETED!
milestone_payload.motivational_quote: 'By the time' ka future trap seekh liya! Ab uski cousin — Future Perfect Continuous dekhte hain.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Sir agar agle mahine mera yahan 5 saal ho jaayenge job karte hue, isko kaise likhenge?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Badhiya sawal! Yahan 'job karna' ek DURATION tak chalta rahega future ke ek point tak. Ye Future Perfect Continuous hai.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Matlab isme bhi 'kitni der se' wala time bataya jaata hai, jaise Present Perfect Continuous mein tha?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Bilkul sahi! Ye tense use hota hai jab kisi action ki DURATION dikhani ho jo future ke ek specific point tak CHALTI RAHEGI.

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Structure: Subject + will have been + V-ing. 'Next month, I will have been working here for five years.'

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Toh 'will have been' hamesha same rehta hai, bas verb-ing badalti hai?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Sahi! Sabhi subjects ke saath 'will have been' hi aata hai — I, You, He, They — sabke saath same, bas verb '-ing' form mein hogi.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Note kar liya — will have been + V-ing, ye teeno words fix hain!

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Yahan bhi wahi Since/For rule chalega jo pehle seekha tha — 'Since' = FIXED POINT (since 2020), 'For' = DURATION (for five years).

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Sir 'By December, he will have been teaching since ten years' sahi hoga kya?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: ⭐ Nahi! Yahi trap phir se aata hai — '10 years' duration hai, isliye 'for' aayega: 'will have been teaching for ten years'. 'Since' hoga tabhi jab fixed point ho, jaise 'since 2014'.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: ⭐ Since/For ka rule toh sabhi 4 continuous-perfect tenses mein SAME hai — Present Perfect Continuous, Future Perfect Continuous, sab mein!

quiz_payload.question: Sahi sentence chuno:

options.text: By next year, she will have been living here since ten years.
By next year, she will have been living here for ten years.
By next year, she has been living here for ten years.
By next year, she will be living here since ten years.

quiz_payload.explanation: 'Ten years' ek duration hai, isliye 'for' aayega, 'since' nahi. Aur 'by next year' + duration ke saath Future Perfect Continuous ('will have been living') sahi structure hai.

quiz_payload.question: Error Detection: 'By the end of this year (A)/ he will have working (B)/ in this company for a decade (C)/ No error (D)'
quiz_payload.explanation: Future Perfect Continuous ka structure 'will have been + V-ing' hai, 'will have working' mein 'been' missing hai. Sahi: 'will have been working'.

quiz_payload.question: Future Perfect Continuous aur Future Perfect mein main difference kya hai?

options.text: Koi farak nahi, dono same hain
Future Perfect completion dikhata hai, Future Perfect Continuous duration/continuation dikhata hai
Future Perfect sirf negative sentences mein aata hai
Future Perfect Continuous sirf questions mein aata hai

quiz_payload.explanation: Future Perfect ('will have+V3') ek kaam ke COMPLETE hone ko dikhata hai, jabki Future Perfect Continuous ('will have been+V-ing') us kaam ki DURATION/continuation ko dikhata hai.

milestone_payload.title: MODULE COMPLETED!
milestone_payload.motivational_quote: Chaaron Future Tenses clear ho gaye Raju! Ab dekhte hain time/if-clause ka sabse bada trap.

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: ⭐ Raju, ab sabse bada exam trap dobara detail mein revise karte hain — Time aur Conditional (if) clauses mein FUTURE TENSE (will) kabhi use NAHI hota, chahe overall meaning future ki ho.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Sir 'If it will rain, we will not go out' — ye sahi hoga na? Dono jagah future feel ho raha hai!

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: ⭐ Yahi galti sabse zyada hoti hai! Sahi hoga: 'If it rains, we will not go out.' 'If' clause mein Simple Present, sirf MAIN clause mein 'will' aata hai.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Hain?? Toh future ki baat karte hue bhi 'if' wale part mein 'will' nahi lagana?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Bilkul sahi Raju! Ye rule sirf 'if' pe nahi, balki sabhi TIME/CONDITIONAL connector words pe lagta hai: when, while, before, after, till, until, as soon as, unless.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Matlab in sabke baad wale clause mein Simple Present hi aayega, chahe future ki baat ho rahi ho?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Exactly! 'When she arrives, we will start.' 'Until he apologizes, I will not talk to him.' 'As soon as the rain stops, we will leave.' — sabme pattern same hai.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: ⭐ Ye toh super important rule hai, isko main pakka yaad rakhunga — connector wale clause mein 'will' kabhi nahi!

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Isko 'If-Clause Type 1' (Real/Possible Future Condition) bhi kehte hain. Structure: If + Simple Present, Subject + will + V1. Ye ek REAL/POSSIBLE future situation dikhata hai.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Sir maine 'If had money, I would buy' jaisa bhi kahin dekha tha, wo alag hai kya?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Haan bilkul alag! Wo Type 2 (unreal/hypothetical present) hota hai jisme 'If+Past Simple, would+V1' aata hai — ye HYPOTHETICAL situation ke liye hai, jo Future Tense chapter ka part nahi, wo separate 'Conditional Sentences' topic hai.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Achha! Toh abhi ke liye sirf Type 1 (real future condition) yaad rakhun — if+present, will+V1!

quiz_payload.question: Sahi sentence chuno:

options.text: When he will come, I will tell him the truth.
When he comes, I will tell him the truth.
When he came, I will tell him the truth.
When he will comes, I will tell him the truth.

quiz_payload.explanation: Time clause ('when') mein future ke liye Simple Present use hota hai, 'will' nahi. Main clause mein 'will tell' sahi hai.

quiz_payload.question: Error Detection: 'Unless you will work hard (A)/ you will not (B)/ succeed in the exam (C)/ No error (D)'
quiz_payload.explanation: 'Unless' ek conditional connector hai, iske clause mein Simple Present aayega, 'will' nahi. Sahi: 'Unless you work hard'.

quiz_payload.question: 'As soon as the meeting ___, I will call you.' Sahi form:
quiz_payload.explanation: 'As soon as' ek time clause connector hai, iske andar future ki baat bhi Simple Present mein likhi jaati hai — 'ends' sahi hai, 'will end' galat.

milestone_payload.title: MODULE COMPLETED!
milestone_payload.motivational_quote: Ye SBI PO ka sabse repeated trap tha aur tumne crack kar liya! Ab dekhte hain 'Future in the Past' ka interesting concept.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Sir, meri mummy ne kaha tha 'Main kal market jaungi' — but wo baat toh AB PAST ho chuki hai, isko kaise likhein?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Bahut interesting sawal Raju! Jab hum PAST mein kisi ke future plan ko REPORT karte hain, 'will' 'WOULD' ban jaata hai — 'Mummy said she would go to the market.'

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Matlab 'will' ka past version 'would' hota hai?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Bilkul sahi! Isko 'Future in the Past' kehte hain — ye ek aisa future action hai jo PAST ke perspective se dekha ja raha hai.

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Ye Reported Speech ka BACKSHIFT rule hai jo tumne Present Tense chapter mein bhi dekha tha. Jab reporting verb Past mein ho (said, told), 'will' → 'would' ban jaata hai, 'shall' → 'should' ban jaata hai.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Sir agar reporting verb Present mein ho, jaise 'says'?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Tab tense change NAHI hota — 'He says, "I will go"' → 'He says that he will go.' Backshift sirf tab hota hai jab reporting verb Past mein ho.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Achha! Toh 'says' ke baad 'will' hi rahega, sirf 'said' ke baad 'would' banega!

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: ⭐ Ek aur zaroori structure — 'Was/Were going to + V1' use hota hai jab past mein koi plan tha, LEKIN wo pura HUA YA NAHI ye clear nahi hota, aksar NAHI HUA hota. 'I was going to call you, but I forgot.'

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Sir matlab ye 'going to' ka past version hai, jaise 'will' ka past 'would' hota hai?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Bilkul sahi! 'Am/is/are going to' (present ka future plan) → 'was/were going to' (past ka future plan) ban jaata hai. Aksar iske saath 'but' aata hai jo bataata hai plan poora nahi hua.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: ⭐ Note kar liya — 'was/were going to + but' = plan tha, lekin hua nahi. Ye toh bahut useful pattern hai!

quiz_payload.question: 'He said that he ___ finish the work by evening.' Sahi form chuno:
quiz_payload.explanation: Reporting verb 'said' Past mein hai, isliye backshift rule ke hisaab se 'will' → 'would' ban jaayega.

quiz_payload.question: Error Detection: 'I (A)/ was going to attend the seminar (B)/ but I will fall sick suddenly (C)/ No error (D)'
quiz_payload.explanation: Ye poora context past mein ho raha hai, isliye 'will fall' galat hai. Sahi: 'but I fell sick suddenly' (Simple Past).

quiz_payload.question: 'He says, "I shall complete the report."' Iska sahi Reported Speech kya hoga?

options.text: He said that he should complete the report.
He says that he shall complete the report.
He says that he should complete the report.
He said that he shall complete the report.

quiz_payload.explanation: Reporting verb 'says' PRESENT mein hai, isliye tense backshift NAHI hoga — 'shall' wahi rahega. Sahi: 'He says that he shall complete the report.'

milestone_payload.title: MODULE COMPLETED!
milestone_payload.completed_topic: Future in the Past (Would / Was Going To)
milestone_payload.motivational_quote: Officer-level grammar mind ban gaya hai tumhara! Ab final module — SBI PO Error Detection Master Practice!

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Ab hum karenge exact SBI PO style practice — sentence 4 parts mein todke error dhundhna. Strategy: 1) 'Will/Shall' ke baad V1 hai ya nahi check karo. 2) Time/if-clause mein 'will' toh nahi ghus gaya?

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Aur kya check karna hai sir?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: 3) Going to/Will ka context sahi hai kya (plan vs spontaneous)? 4) Double modal error toh nahi (will+can jaisa)? 5) Since/For sahi jagah hai kya?

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Ye toh ek poori checklist ban gayi sir! Chaliye practice karte hain!

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Trap 1: Double Modal Error. Do modals ek saath kabhi nahi aa sakte — 'He will can go' GALAT hai, kyunki 'will' aur 'can' dono modal hain.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Toh sahi kya hoga sir?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Sahi hoga: 'He will be able to go' — 'can' ki jagah 'be able to' use karte hain jab 'will' ke saath ability dikhani ho. Ye BPSC ka classic trap hai.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Achhaaaa! Modal ke baad direct verb aani chahiye, dusra modal nahi!

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Trap 2: 'Will' aur 'Going to' ko MIX karna. 'I will going to visit him' GALAT hai — dono future markers ek saath nahi aa sakte.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Toh ya toh 'will visit' ya 'am going to visit' — dono ek saath nahi?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Bilkul sahi! Sirf ek future-expression method use karo per sentence. 'I will visit him' YA 'I am going to visit him' — dono correct, mix karna galat.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Note kar liya — ek sentence mein ek hi future marker!

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Trap 3: Time-clause mein 'will' — ye sabse zyada repeat hone wala error hai. 'I will call you when I will reach home' — dono jagah 'will' lagana GALAT hai.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Sahi hoga 'I will call you when I reach home' — sirf main clause mein 'will'?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Ekdum sahi Raju! Time-clause word (when/if/before/after/till/until/as soon as/unless) ke baad hamesha Simple Present, sirf main clause mein 'will'.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: ⭐ Ye rule ab pakka set ho gaya dimaag mein!

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Trap 4: Present Perfect/Present time markers ke saath Future Tense ka mix. 'I will meet him yesterday' jaisa GALAT sentence bhi exam mein dikhaya jaata hai.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Hain?? 'Yesterday' ke saath 'will' kaise chalega, wo toh past hai!

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: ⭐ Bilkul sahi pakda! 'Yesterday' ek DEFINITE PAST marker hai, isliye 'will' (future) ke saath kabhi nahi aa sakta. Sahi: 'I met him yesterday' — hamesha time marker check karo, verb usse match honi chahiye.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Toh time marker aur tense ka mismatch dhundhna hi sabse pehla step hai error detection mein!

quiz_payload.question: Error Detection: 'She (A)/ will can complete (B)/ the assignment by tomorrow (C)/ No error (D)'
quiz_payload.explanation: Do modals ('will' aur 'can') ek saath use nahi ho sakte. Sahi: 'will be able to complete'.

quiz_payload.question: Error Detection: 'If you will study hard (A)/ you will definitely (B)/ crack the BPSC exam (C)/ No error (D)'
quiz_payload.explanation: 'If' clause mein future ke liye Simple Present aata hai, 'will' nahi. Sahi: 'If you study hard'.

quiz_payload.question: Error Detection: 'I (A)/ will going to submit (B)/ my resignation letter tomorrow (C)/ No error (D)'
quiz_payload.explanation: 'Will' aur 'going to' dono future markers ek saath mix nahi ho sakte. Sahi: 'am going to submit' ya 'will submit'.

revision_points.point: Statement I: Traditional rule mein 'shall' first person (I/We) ke saath, 'will' baaki subjects ke saath aata hai. Statement II: Formal offers ('Shall I help?') aur strong command/promise ('You shall not pass') mein 'shall' second/third person ke saath bhi sahi hai. Dono statements sahi hain — exception hamesha exam mein poocha jaata hai.

revision_points.topic: Statement Check: Going to vs Will
revision_points.point: Statement I: Pre-decided plans ke liye 'going to' use hota hai, spontaneous decisions ke liye 'will'. Statement II: Evidence-based prediction mein 'going to' (kaale baadal dekh ke), opinion-based prediction mein 'will'. Dono statements sahi hain — context hi decide karta hai.

Statement I: If/when/before/after/till/until/unless/as soon as wale clause mein future ke liye Simple Present aata hai. Statement II: Main clause mein 'will' aata hai. Dono statements sahi hain — clause mein 'will' dekhna hamesha error hai.

Statement I: 'By/By the time' + future point ke saath 'will have+V3' complete hone wala kaam dikhata hai. Statement II: 'By the time' clause mein bhi Simple Present hi aayega (future meaning ke liye), Future Perfect nahi. Dono statements sahi hain.

revision_points.topic: Statement Check: Future in the Past
revision_points.point: Statement I: Reporting verb Past mein ho to 'will'→'would', 'shall'→'should' backshift hota hai. Statement II: Reporting verb Present mein ho to backshift nahi hota. Dono statements sahi hain — 'was/were going to' bhi past ka unfulfilled plan dikhata hai.

quiz_payload.question: Assertion-Reason: Assertion (A): 'By the time he reaches the office, the meeting will have started' is grammatically correct. Reason (R): In 'by the time' constructions with future reference, the time clause takes Simple Present while the main clause takes Future Perfect.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

quiz_payload.explanation: 'Reaches' (Simple Present for future meaning) is correctly used in the 'by the time' clause, and 'will have started' (Future Perfect) correctly shows the earlier-completing action. Both Assertion and Reason are true and R correctly explains A.

quiz_payload.question: Multi-Statement: Read the sentence and find which parts contain an error: 'If it will rain heavily tomorrow (A) / the farmers will be knowing (B) / that the crops will have been saved (C) / No error (D)'. Choose the part(s) with error.
quiz_payload.explanation: Part A error: 'If' clause requires Simple Present, not 'will' — should be 'If it rains heavily tomorrow'. Part B error: 'Know' is a stative verb, cannot take continuous form — should be 'the farmers will know'. Part C is actually correct in this future-perfect-continuous-style context showing a completed future state.

quiz_payload.question: BPSC Style: Consider the following statements about Future Tense usage: (1) 'Shall I open the window?' is grammatically correct as a formal offer. (2) 'I will going to meet him tomorrow' is grammatically correct. (3) 'Look at the sky, it is going to rain' correctly uses evidence-based prediction. Which of the statements is/are CORRECT?
quiz_payload.explanation: Statement 1 is CORRECT — 'Shall I' is the standard formal offer structure. Statement 2 is WRONG — 'will' and 'going to' cannot be mixed in one sentence. Statement 3 is CORRECT — visible evidence (dark sky) correctly triggers 'going to' for prediction. So statements 1 and 3 are correct.

quiz_payload.question: Error Detection (SBI PO Level): Find the part with error: 'The manager announced (A) / that the company would launch (B) / a new product next year (C) / No error (D)'
quiz_payload.explanation: This sentence is correct as written. 'Announced' is a Past reporting verb, so the backshift rule correctly changes 'will launch' to 'would launch' in reported speech, representing 'Future in the Past'.
